summary: Viktor Iosifovich Balin worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University from circa 1946 to 1951 and taught there in 1952.

Vilgelm Mikhailovich Berner was an Indologist. He studied at the Leningrad Oriental Institute in 1931 and served as an aspirant at the Institute of Anthropology, Moscow State University, from 1935 to 1936.

Vilhelm Peter Grønbech was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He earned his cand.mag. at the University of Copenhagen (1890–1897), studying under Vilhelm Thomsen, Karl Verner, and Holger Pedersen, and later held docentships there and taught at Danmarks Lærerhøjskole.

Vilhelm Thomsen was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. Educated at the University of Copenhagen under Johan Nicolai Madvig and Niels Ludvig Westergaard, he served there as Privatdozent and Professor (1887–1913).

Vilhelm Trenckner specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen in 1841 under Johan Nicolai Madvig, Christian Thorning Engelstoft Hermansen, and Niels Ludvig Westergaard, and later taught at Det Kgl. Vajsenhus in 1860.

Ville Husgafvel works in religious and Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki (2015–2023), was a visiting research student at SOAS (2017–2018), and served as a project researcher at Helsinki from 2022 to 2023.

Vimla Karnatak works in Indology and philosophy. She studied under Gajanan Shastri Musalgaonkar and served as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit at Banaras Hindu University (attested 2000).

Vinay Lal is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Johns Hopkins University (circa 1980–1982) and became a professor in the Department of History and Asian American Studies at UCLA around 1993.

Vinaya Kshirsagar specializes in Indology and linguistics. She was a professor at Dr. D. Y. Patil Medical College, Hospital & Research Centre in 2015 and is attested in 2026 as Professor-Editor of the Sanskrit Dictionary at Deccan College.

Vincenc Lesný was an Indologist, Buddhist scholar, and Iranian and Central Asian studies specialist. Educated at Charles University, Oxford, and Bonn under Josef Zubatý, Moriz Winternitz, Arthur Anthony Macdonell, and Hermann Jacobi, he became a professor at Charles University.

Vincenc Pořízka worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Palacký University Olomouc and Charles University under Vincenc Lesný and Otakar Pertold, and held posts at the University of Chicago, Charles University, and Humboldt University of Berlin.

Vincent Arthur Smith was a historian and Indologist who studied at Trinity College Dublin and Cambridge. He served in the Indian Civil Service, as Reader in Indian History at Dublin and Oxford, and as Curator of the Indian Institute.

Vincent Breugem is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden University (MA and PhD), Taisho, Kyoto, and Hanazono Universities, as well as under Lucia Dolce, and held a research fellowship at Leiden University.

Vincent Eltschinger specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at Lausanne, Fribourg, and Vienna under Tom Tillemans, he held posts at Lausanne, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Vincent Goossaert is a scholar of sinology and religious studies who studied under Kristofer Schipper. He held posts at the CNRS (circa 1998–2012), The Chinese University of Hong Kong (2007), and École Pratique des Hautes Études (circa 2012).

Vincent Lefèvre specializes in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at École Nationale des Chartes and Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Bruno Dagens, and has served as a curator at the Guimet Museum.

Vincent Tournier specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at EPHE and Leiden University under Seishi Karashima and Cristina Scherrer-Schaub, holding appointments at Sciences Po Grenoble, EFEO, Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the University of Tokyo.

Vincenz Scherzl was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Charles University, King's College London, Saint Petersburg State University under Kaetan Andreevich Kossovich, and Moscow State University, later serving as professor of comparative linguistics at Kharkiv and Odesa Universities.

Vincenzo Vergiani is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied under Raffaele Torella between circa 1997 and 2003, and was appointed Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Cambridge in 2007.

Vinit Deo specializes in Indology, history and archaeology, and philosophy. He completed an MA in Indology at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (2022–2024) and was an alumnus of Indira Gandhi National Open University in 2024.
